exact_statement: For all a>=1 and even m>=2, let F_{a,m} be the disjoint product of a bent/one-point-flip Boolean splices defined in REPORT.md. With delta=2^-m, J=m/2+m*delta and I0=J+delta, I(F)=a*I0 and I_sel=a*delta. The full-set mask costs a(m+1)<=3I(F), and the explicitly conditioned single-root queue reference, including empty-sector entropy and exact elementary-symmetric normalizers, has complete cost <9I(F). For each fixed a as m tends to infinity, mask/I->2, queue/I->2G, mask/Delta~2^m and queue/Delta~G*2^m, with G defined in REPORT.md and 1<=G<=1+(3/5)(1-1/(2ln2)). On the actual selector-first tree stopping after selectors, the expected raw 2I(D_v) boundary charge is a*m*delta+delta*a(a-1)(2J+delta). For every fixed finite bad-node threshold K, choose even m with m-1>K; all selector nodes obey B_v>K Inf_v, but this raw-charge/I ratio grows unboundedly with a. Removing exact independent tensor spectators leaves charge a*m*delta<=I(F)/2. This rejects the specified raw selector-first budget only, not existence of a universal adaptive tree or FEI.
